title: F1 (6V max) and CR1 (VBR~7.2-8V, pulse-rated only) are both under-margined against a sustained 9-20V VBUS fault
refs: sibling scratch wf/protection/FINDINGS.md: F1 rated max voltage 6V; CR1 VBR 7.22-7.98V min, Vc 11.2V@17.9A (pulse); TP4056 VCC abs max 8V; TPS2116 VIN1/MODE abs max 6V
location: J1/CR1/F1/U11.VCC/U2.VIN1,MODE, board coords CR1 (92.90,100.20), F1 (94.41,94.27)
evidence: CR1 SMF6.5CA's published ratings (VBR, Vc@17.9A) are standard TVS pulse-clamp ratings for a short surge (typ. 10x1000us), not a continuous-DC power spec; its SOD-123FL package has no meaningful continuous power budget at multi-volt avalanche conduction. F1's own datasheet caps its working voltage at 6V. Neither part is specified for a sustained fault in the 9-20V range (a class of fault this USB2.0-only, non-PD, D+/D--wired-to-ESP32 board cannot itself prevent, since it never negotiates voltage over CC and has no BC1.2 D+/D- signaling to decline legacy fast-charge protocols).
jlc_build: same as handbuild - CR1 (hongjiacheng) and F1 (Brightking) are already established as electrically identical to the prime Littelfuse parts, so both builds share this exposure identically.
recommendation: For a genuine sustained overvoltage fault: if CR1 fails short (plausible, likely outcome under sustained avalanche overstress), F1's PTC should trip and isolate downstream ICs — an acceptable but sacrificial fail-safe requiring board rework afterward. If CR1 instead fails open, F1 (6V-rated) is left to interrupt/carry the full 9-20V fault it isn't rated for, and the fault can reach TP4056 VCC (8V abs max) and TPS2116 VIN1/MODE (6V abs max) largely unclamped. Consider a higher-voltage-rated crowbar/OVP stage (or a PTC/TVS pair explicitly rated for the fast-charge voltage range) if exposure to non-compliant/legacy-fast-charge USB-C sources is a real concern for this product; otherwise document the residual risk. This is additive to, not a duplicate of, the already-established hot-plug-transient/6V-abs-max finding, which covers only microsecond-scale ringing, not a sustained fault.

title: Fix 4 CE gate cannot start the charger when J5 shows <~1-1.8 V: a pack whose own protection has tripped (0 V) or a deeply drained bare cell can never be recharged on-board
evidence: Netlist: U11.8 CE is driven only by Q2.D (R82 1M to GND); Q2.G=/DET_NODE is pulled low only by Q9, whose gate is R79 100k/R80 1M across J5 (Vgs=0.909*V(J5)), source=B-. With CE low nothing can raise P+/B+: TPS2116 blocks VOUT->VIN2, TP4056 BAT <=2 uA in shutdown (C16581 sheet), loads on P+ ~6 uA. A LiPo pack with built-in PCM in over-discharge lockout presents ~0 V at its leads (discharge FET off; the board's 0.5 MOhm across J5 pulls the terminals together), so Q9 stays off forever. Same for a bare cell that keeps draining after the on-board cutoff (R56/57 + R79/80 + DW01A ~7-11 uA, plus ~3 uA of a pack PCM) until 0.909*Vcell < Vth. Before Fix 4 (CE tied to VBUS) the charger always applied voltage and revived such packs. docs/HARDWARE.md:101 still states 'a pack with its own protection also works - the two cascade'. DESIGN_REVIEW only lists '0 V pack: recovery not guaranteed' under the superseded alternative, not under Fix 4. Packs whose PCM trips at 2.7-3.0 V will always trip before the on-board DW01A (2.4/2.5 V).
jlc_build: hongjiacheng BSS138 Vth 0.8/1.2/1.6 V -> charger enable needs 0.9-1.76 V across J5. PUOLOP DW01A supports 0-V charging (start 1.2 V), so a manual CE override would revive a pack.
handbuild: onsemi BSS138L Vth 0.5-1.5 V -> needs 0.55-1.65 V. Fortune DW01A-G has NO 0-V charge function (V0INH 1.5 V), so even a manual CE override may not open the charge FET for a 0 V pack; external charger needed.
recommendation: Decide before ordering: (a) minimum - correct HARDWARE.md/README (tripped or 0 V packs are not recoverable on-board) and have firmware stop/deep-sleep early (>=3.3 V) with a 'charge now' warning; (b) zero-BOM-cost layout aid - add a normally-open solder jumper / two test pads /DET_NODE-to-GND labelled FORCE CHG so a user with verified polarity can kick the charger (self-holds once the pack wakes); (c) next spin - a deliberate high-impedance wake path. Add 'tripped protected pack + USB' to the section-13 bench list.

title: TLV75533 + TPS2116 leave near-zero headroom to ESP32-S3's 3.0V min at realistic (non-empty) battery voltages under WiFi-TX load
location: netlist nets LDO_IN, 3V3, P+; schematic power section (TPS2116 VIN2=P+ -> VOUT=LDO_IN -> U3 IN/EN -> 3V3 -> U4 pin2)
evidence: TLV755P datasheet (tlv755p_ti.txt): VDO at IOUT=500mA, 3.3V<=VOUT<5.0V bin, DBV package, -40..85C = 150mV typ / 215mV max. TPS2116 datasheet: RON = 37/46 mOhm typ/max @25C, up to 55 mOhm max over -40..85C. ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet: Operating voltage/power supply = 3.0-3.6V (line 66). Netlist confirms U3.EN is hard-tied to U3.IN (both on net LDO_IN) - the LDO has no shutdown/enable margin control, it simply follows LDO_IN. Chain math at VBAT=3.3V (a state well above a typical Li-ion protection IC's over-discharge cutoff, i.e. NOT yet an 'empty' battery by fuel-gauge standards) under a 350-500mA WiFi-TX current pulse (per task-given spec): LDO_IN = VBAT - I*(TPS2116 RON, ~27.5mV @500mA) - protection-FET drop (tens of mOhm, per already-established FET-equivalence work) approx 3.15-3.2V. Required VIN for full regulation at 500mA = 3.3V + 215mV(max VDO) = 3.515V. Actual VIN is ~300-350mV short, so the LDO is already in dropout, and its output tracks VIN minus its dropout (worst case ~150-215mV) -> 3V3 rail sags to roughly 2.9-3.05V, at or below the WROOM-1's 3.0V minimum operating voltage.
jlc_build: same both builds - LCSC C404027 verified genuine TI TLV75533PDBVR (productModel/brand confirmed via LCSC API), and TPS2116DRLR (LCSC C3235557) is the prime part on both BOMs; the analysis is identical.
recommendation: Bench-verify 3V3 rail sag with a battery-voltage power supply (not just a fresh battery) swept from 4.2V down to 3.3V while pulsing WiFi TX, watching for brownout resets. If margin is confirmed thin, consider: (a) a lower-dropout/lower-RON path (larger battery-side FETs or a dedicated ORing diode/FET sized for lower Vf), (b) setting the firmware's discharge cutoff / low-battery shutdown well above 3.3V so the pack is disconnected before this region is reached, or (c) an LDO/buck with lower VDO at 500mA.

title: Button ADC ladders' idle level and top codes sit above the ESP32-S3's spec'd ADC calibration range
refs: ESP32-S3 datasheet v2.2, scratch/wf/esp32-ldo-power/esp32s3_chip.txt lines ~5074-5096 (Table 5-6 ADC Calibration Results: ATTEN3 effective measurement range 0-2900mV, error +-50mV max)
netlist.xml: R4/R28 (10k pull-ups to 3V3), R60/R18/R19/R20 (ADC_1 branches 100/5.6k/20k/56k), R61/R11/R35/R36 (ADC_2 branches 100/12k/33k/68k)
location: BUTTON_ADC_1 (U4/ESP32-S3 pin 39, IO1) and BUTTON_ADC_2 (U4 pin 4, IO4); resistors R4,R60,R18,R19,R20,R28,R61,R11,R35,R36
evidence: Both ladders use a 10k pull-up to 3V3 with branch resistors to GND when a button is pressed. Computed Vadc = 3.3V*Rb/(Rb+10k): idle (no button pressed) = 3300 mV on both lines; highest-code buttons are SW9 (R20=56k) = 2800 mV on ADC_1 and SW7 (R36=68k) = 2877 mV on ADC_2. The ESP32-S3 datasheet's only attenuation setting that reaches anywhere near 3.3V is ATTEN3 (11dB), and its calibrated/spec'd 'effective measurement range' is explicitly listed as 0-2900mV with +-50mV max error (10x worse than ATTEN0's +-5mV) - inputs above ~2900mV are outside Espressif's characterized/guaranteed-linear region. The idle state (3300mV, used on both lines) is unconditionally above this ceiling, and SW7 (2877mV) sits right at the edge of it.
jlc_build: same both builds (ESP32-S3 module + resistor ladder values are identical regardless of LCSC vs DigiKey sourcing; this is a fixed-value analog design margin issue)
recommendation: Lower the ladder's top-of-range design voltage with headroom below 2900mV (e.g. rescale so idle sits near ~2.5-2.7V and the highest code is a few hundred mV below that), or confirm in firmware/first-article testing that idle and SW7/SW9 remain reliably distinguishable using ADC oneshot with calibration enabled at the top of its range. Not a functional blocker (a saturated/compressed but still monotonic ADC region can usually still be decoded with wide firmware thresholds), but it removes analog margin exactly where the ladder currently needs it most (adjacent-code spacing near the top is only 344-500 mV, comparable to the possible top-of-range error).

title: Battery path is routed entirely in 0.20-0.25 mm tracks with a 0603 0R jumper, but the DW01A over-current trip is 2.1-4.4 A, so the protection does not protect the board's own battery path
location: Nets B- (all 34.97 mm at 0.20 mm, B.Cu, J5.1 94.85,67.50 -> Q1.1 ~86.6,72), B+ (29.6 mm at 0.25 mm), P+ (82 mm at 0.25 mm, 2.09 mm at 0.20), Net-(Q3-D)/Net-(Q8-D) 0.25 mm, R27 (91.56,77.84); no zones on any of these nets

Trip current = V_OCP / Rss(on): PUOLOP 130/150/170 mV over TECH PUBLIC 2 x (19.5 typ..31.5 max) mOhm = 2.06..4.4 A, typ ~3.5 A; Fortune DW01A-G + FS8205: 120..180 mV / 46..74 mOhm = 1.6..3.9 A. title: Entire battery power loop is routed at 0.20-0.25 mm with a 0603 0-ohm jumper in series, while the only over-current limit is the DW01A at ~1.6-4 A / 10-20 ms
evidence: pcbnew: no zones on B+/B-/P+; widths B- 0.2 mm, B+ 0.25 mm, P+ 0.25/0.2 mm. deep3: B+ 29.4 mOhm, B- 29.0 mOhm, P+ 28-37 mOhm; loop ~0.3 ohm with Q3/Q8/Q1/R27 (0.17 V at 0.5 A - fine for normal use). Fault case: P+ is exposed unfused on J6.12; a short there gives ~4.2 V/(~0.47 ohm incl. cell) ~ 9 A, which is only ~0.5 V across Q1 - below the DW01A short threshold (1.0-1.7 V), so the slow over-current timer (10-20 ms) applies. 9 A for 20 ms in a 0.2 mm x 35 um trace is ~160 C adiabatic rise; R27 (0603 thick-film jumper, 1 A rated) takes the same pulse. IPC-2221: 0.2 mm outer trace carries ~0.74 A for 10 C rise, ~2 A for ~100 C - i.e. a sustained overload just under the DW01A trip cooks the trace.

title: Reverse-battery safety relies on 1 MOhm bias against unguaranteed leakage: R82 vs Q2 IDSS and unknown CE bias, R81 vs DET_NODE leakage
location: /DET_NODE (6.8 mm, 0.2 mm track) and CE (8.4 mm) on B.Cu around (88-95, 83-94)
evidence: AO3401A datasheet: IDSS max -1 uA at 25 C, -5 uA at 55 C (VDS -30 V), Vth min -0.5 V at 250 uA. With the detector OFF (reversed/no cell) CE is held low only by R82 = 1 MOhm: 1 uA -> 1 V, 3.3 uA -> CE fully high. The TP4056 sheet gives no CE threshold or input current ('TTL or CMOS'); the lead's own deck assumes ~1.0-1.2 V. On the gate side, 0.3-0.5 uA of leakage on /DET_NODE (Q9 IDSS max 0.5 uA per hongjiacheng sheet, flux residue under SOT-23) drops 0.3-0.5 V across R81 = Q2 Vgs near min Vth, and Q2 only has to source ~1-3 uA to lift CE. A false CE-high with a reversed cell recreates the 0.25 A reverse-charge fault Fix 4 exists to prevent. Typical silicon leakage at 3.3 V is nA-level, so this is a guaranteed-margin gap, not an expected failure.
jlc_build: hongjiacheng BSS138 IDSS <=0.5 uA @50 V; JLC no-clean flux residue on 1 MOhm nodes is the realistic contributor.
handbuild: onsemi BSS138L IDSS 0.1 uA @25 V / 0.5 uA @50 V; hand-solder flux residue likely heavier - clean the Q2/Q9/R81/R82 area with IPA.
recommendation: Stiffen the OFF state: R82 -> 100k and R81 -> 330k-470k (free if Q2/R81 are re-sourced from USB_VBUS per the previous finding; otherwise weigh +uA). Bench: with no cell and with a current-limited reversed emulator, measure CE (<0.3 V required) at room temperature and ~50 C.

title: Always-on LDO (EN tied to IN) and un-gated battery-monitor divider make non-MCU leakage the dominant term in deep-sleep/standby current draw
location: netlist net LDO_IN (U3 EN=IN) and net BAT_MONIT (R12 1M from P+, R10 1M to GND, U4.IO8)
evidence: TLV755P datasheet: IGND (ground current) = 25uA typ / 31uA max @25C, up to 40uA max @125C, IOUT=0 - and since U3.EN is wired to U3.IN (no external enable control), this current flows continuously whenever LDO_IN is powered (i.e. whenever USB or battery is present), independent of ESP32 deep-sleep state. R10/R12 form a 1M+1M=2M resistive divider wired directly, unswitched, across P+ (battery, post-protection) to GND for BAT_MONIT (IO8/ADC1) - continuous drain = VBAT/2M = ~1.85uA at 3.7V nominal, ~2.1uA at 4.2V full charge, present even during deep sleep or when the board is otherwise idle. ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 datasheet Table 6-7 (Current Consumption in Low-Power Modes): Deep-sleep with RTC memory powered / RTC peripherals down = 7uA typ; with RTC peripherals also up = 8uA typ. So the LDO's own IQ (25-40uA) alone is 3-5x the chip's own deep-sleep current, and the always-on divider adds another ~25% on top of the chip's deep-sleep budget.
jlc_build: same both builds - R10/R12 (LCSC C22935, Yageo 1M 0603) and U3 are identical prime/LCSC parts on both BOMs.
recommendation: If long-duration battery standby (weeks/months) matters for this e-reader, consider gating the BAT_MONIT divider with a small FET (only enable it briefly when sampling) and/or using a lower-IQ or switch-controlled power path for the 3V3 rail (e.g. a load switch gated by a GPIO before deep sleep) so total idle current is not dominated by fixed analog leakage. If standby time is not a design goal (e.g. device is always charged/active), this can be accepted as-is.

title: In any DW01A lockout the system GND floats up to P+, which turns Q8 off (gate = GND): battery-only start needs Vcell >= VODR + ~0.3 V, and an over-current trip never self-releases; USB is the only way back

title: L2 saturates (Isat 1.0 A max-spec) below the TPS923610 cycle-by-cycle limit (1.6-2.1 A); fine in normal operation, no margin in transients/faults

evidence: TDK VLS252012HBX-100M-1 (ds/tdk_vls252012hbx_lcsc.txt table row): 10 uH ±20%, DCR 0.45 typ/0.54 max, Isat 1.00 A max-spec (1.30 typ, 30% L drop), Itemp 0.85 A. TPS923610 DS: ILIM 1.6/1.8/2.1 A, ILIM_START 0.8 A, Fsw 1.1 MHz. Operating point Vin 3.0 V, Vout 15 V, 13.3 mA, eta 0.8: IL_DC = 83 mA, ripple = 1/(L*(1/(Vout-Vin)+1/Vin)*Fs) = 0.218 A pp, Ipk ~0.19 A (5x below Isat). Start-up limit 0.8 A < Isat. Only an output short/large step (colour switch to a much higher-Vf string, OVP recovery) drives current to ILIM, where L has already collapsed and the peak overshoots the 1.8 A limit during the comparator blanking.
jlc_build: same both builds (C88532 is genuine TDK)
recommendation: Acceptable for a 13 mA load; if a larger Isat is wanted at the same footprint, TDK VLS252012HBX-4R7M-1 (higher Isat, more ripple) or a 3.0x3.0 part; otherwise just note it. No BOM change required.

title: LED+ (LED_SW) on J6.5/TP3 has no short-circuit protection: a short to GND is a direct LDO_IN short through L2 and U10's body diode

A slip of a probe/jumper on the 2.54 mm header from LED+ to the adjacent GND pin draws roughly (Vin-0.7)/0.7 ohm = 3-5 A, limited only by the TPS2116/PTC on USB or the DW01A overcurrent on battery, through a 0.20-0.25 mm track, and browns out 3V3.

title: Hard short on P+ is unlikely to reach the DW01A short-circuit threshold; it is cleared by the slower 150 mV tier after 7-20 ms while Q8 falls back to its body diode
location: Battery path J5 -> Q3 -> R27 -> Q8 -> P+ ; return GND -> Q1 -> B-
evidence: Short tier needs V_CS >= 0.82 V (PUOLOP min; 1.0 V Fortune) across Q1 Rss ~45 mOhm = 18-22 A (typ 1.36 V = 30 A). Loop resistance tracks ~0.10 + Q3/Q8 ~0.11 + Q1 0.045 + R27/J5 ~0.05 + cell ESR 0.05-0.1 ohm limits a 4.2 V dead short to ~11-14 A, i.e. V_CS ~0.5-0.6 V: above VEDI, below Vshort, so the fault lasts TEDI 7 ms typ / 20 ms max. With P+ shorted to GND, Q8 Vgs (GND - P+) collapses to ~0 so Q8 conducts through its body diode (Vf ~1 V x ~11 A ~ 10 W for up to 20 ms; AO3401A Is rating 2 A continuous). Adiabatic heating of the 0.20 mm B- track at 11 A: ~86 C in 7 ms, ~250 C in 20 ms (dT = I^2*rho*t/(A^2*cv), A = 0.007 mm2).
jlc_build: Same both builds; survivable as a single event but marginal at the 20 ms maximum delay.
handbuild: Same (Fortune TOI1 10 ms typ / 20 ms max).
recommendation: Wider battery tracks (see batt-path-traces-vs-ocp) remove the concern; include a dead-short test on P+ with a current probe in the DESIGN_REVIEW section 13 bench list.

title: TPS923610 latches off after three OVP trips: selecting an absent string or running without the frontlight FPC leaves the driver dead until ADIM is cycled
location: U10 (49.5,122.0); nets LED_SW, COLOR_SEL, LED_MONIT
evidence: Datasheet 7.3.6: when VOUT exceeds OVP (24.25-25.5 V) three times the part enters over-voltage protection mode and does not resume until ADIM is held low >2.5 ms (shutdown) or VIN UVLO. The board supports panels with no light, single-colour (FL01C-class) and dual strings; with COLOR_SEL pointing at a missing string, or J3 empty, enabling ADIM drives LED_SW to ~25 V three times then latches. C9 then bleeds only through R39+R41 (1.12 M, tau ~1.1 s). During that event LED_SW exceeds the JLC-build D8 clone's 24 V standoff only on C-/W- if a string is present on the other channel (cathode sits at LED_SW minus string Vf, so it stays well below 24 V): benign.
jlc_build: same both builds
recommendation: No hardware change. Firmware/docs: after enabling, read LED_MONIT; if it reads ~2.6-2.7 V (OVP) treat as open string, pull ADIM low >2.5 ms to re-arm, and do not blend COLOR_SEL onto a string that is not fitted.

title: USB/charge-status ADC divider (CHRG/STDBY/ST -> IO9) is fully verified correct against all 4 documented voltage windows
refs: netlist.xml: R70(100k,USB_STAT-3V3), R67(56k,CHRG-USB_STAT), R71(22k,STDBY-USB_STAT), R17(150k,ST-USB_STAT), C23(2.2n,USB_STAT-GND), U4.17=IO9
wf/esp32-ldo-power/tps2116_ti.txt line ~1136-1140: 'ST pin...pulled low when VIN1 is not being used...When TPS2116 is powering...using VIN1...ST pin will be pulled high'
schematic note at (477.52,138.43): USB/CHARGE STATUS ADC DIVIDER NOTE with the 4 documented voltage windows
evidence: Thevenin calc for each state exactly matches the documented windows: all Hi-Z -> 3.30V (Idle, >3.10V); CHRG low only -> 3.3*56/156=1.184V (Charging, 1.00-1.35V); STDBY low only -> 3.3*22/122=0.595V (Done, 0.50-0.70V); ST low only -> 3.3*150/250=1.98V (Unplugged/VIN2, 1.70-2.20V). Per TPS2116 datasheet, ST is released (Hi-Z) whenever VIN1/USB is selected -- including while actively charging -- so CHRG and ST can never both assert simultaneously, avoiding an ambiguous double-pulldown reading. IO9 = ADC1_CH8 on ESP32-S3, a WiFi-safe ADC1 channel, and the divider top is only ever 3V3 so the GPIO's 3.3V abs max is never exceeded.
jlc_build: same both builds - purely a resistor network, identical parts both builds.
recommendation: No action needed; this is a well-designed, self-consistent circuit. Recorded here as a verified-correct confirmation for this pre-order review, not a defect.
